token.label: token
token.comment: Fuses two places: tokens are shared. Resource coupling.

cites.note: ns:TokenPatternLink axioms: from is not an in-port, to is not an out-port
linkLegal: both nets must count tokens

data.label: data
data.comment: Fuses two places for read-only observation; the observer may not consume from or produce into the observed place (E_DATALINK_CONSUMES). Legal between any net kinds.

event.label: event
event.comment: Fuses two transitions: when one fires, the other fires too, atomically. No port-direction rule.

cites.note: ns:EventPatternLink axioms: both ends are transition ports
fusion over equivalence classes, so it is associative

guard.label: guard
guard.comment: Gates a transition in one subnet on a place in another (inhibitor or read arc, or a guard conjunct). Restrictive: properties proved of the gated net alone may no longer hold.

cites.note: lowering: "> 0" becomes a read arc of weight 1

link_style_cite.note: linkStyles: color, style and glyph per link kind

queue.definition: A bounded or unbounded buffer. An enqueue transition moves a token into the items place and a dequeue transition takes one out; a bounded queue adds a slots place holding the free capacity.
queue.intent: things arrive and wait until a consumer takes them; optionally with a limit on how many can wait
caveats: Capacity 0 means unbounded: there is no slots place and enqueue becomes a source transition. The net then fails StructuralBoundedness and Validate reports W_UNBOUNDED_QUEUE; bound it from outside, usually by fusing enqueue with a producer whose own net is bounded.
The items place is a counter. The net does not order items, so first-in-first-out is not a property of this pattern; with a payload the items are told apart by item_id only.
Initial greater than a non-zero capacity is rejected with an error (NewQueue), because it would give a negative slot count.

ports.comment: Place items. Token link: a producer pushes work.
Place items. Token link: a consumer pulls work.
Place items. Data or guard link: observe the backlog.
Transition enqueue. Event link: fire together with a producer, so produce-and-enqueue is one atomic firing.
Transition dequeue. Event link: fire together with a consumer.

resource-pool.definition: A fixed number of interchangeable units. acquire moves a unit from available to in_use and release moves it back, so the total never changes.
resource-pool.intent: at most N things can use something at once; each use takes one unit and gives it back
caveats: in_use is an anonymous count. The pool does not record which job holds a unit, so it cannot say that a given job released it.

The available port is tagged `resource`, the same tag a workflow's resource:<id> ports carry, but a saga's account ports are tagged `account`: a port-to-port token link between a pool and a saga is rejected with E_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.
NewResourcePool does not check capacity; a negative or zero value is not rejected in the source read.

altLabel: must be reversed if it fails
saga.definition: An ordered list of steps, each paired with a compensation. One control token walks the steps forward; a failure hands it to a chain that runs the compensations in reverse. Steps move tokens between accounts and the compensation moves them back.
saga.intent: a multi-step business transaction where, if a later step fails, the earlier ones must be undone
saga.constructor: saga.New(id) with Account, SharedAccount, Step, Move, Compensate, MustBuild or BuildValidated, then (*Saga).ToMetaSubnet()
caveats: Saga needs weighted arcs, so it exists only on the metamodel layer.
One saga is one case: the control token is consumed once. Handling many orders takes one saga subnet per order, or a model that carries case identity; this pattern does not.

A refund is the compensation of a step that moved tokens. It runs when a later step fails or when the final acknowledgement fails (fail_commit compensates every step, including the last). A step that fails itself moved nothing, so there is nothing to refund.
A saga with a shared account is not closed, so it declares no conservation constraint of its own; the law is a property of the composite.
The net kind is ResourceNet, so nothing in the legality matrix stops a token link on a control place. Only the account ports are meant for token links.

The account ports are tagged `account`; a ResourcePool's are tagged `resource`. A port-to-port token link between them is rejected (E_SCHEMA_MISMATCH). The saga tests link a shared account to a plain place with no port, which skips the tag check.
completed and rolled_back are out-ports on places. No port fires on 'either outcome', so a transition that must happen on both (for example releasing a worker) cannot be fused with one port.

portTemplates.comment: Token link: share a balance with another subnet instead of duplicating it.
Terminal place: the saga ran to the end.
Terminal place: every step that ran was compensated.
Fuse with the external confirmation, for example a chain's.
Final acknowledgement fails; compensate every step.
Fuse a step with the external action it stands for.
The step fails: it is marked failed and the control token turns round.

invariants.expr: sum of tokens over every control place == 1
sum of tokens over the accounts the steps touch == their summed initial balance
invariants.presentWhen: no touched account is shared, and at least one step moves tokens

idioms.rationale: Fuse dequeue with acquire: an item leaves the queue only at the instant a worker is free, as one atomic firing.
idioms.caveat: Fusion makes one transition consuming from items and available. Check with sim_verify that the composite still has the conservation constraints you expect.

idioms.rationale: Taking an order off the queue and running the saga's first step are one firing. The do:<step> template is instantiated with the first step's id.
idioms.caveat: A saga is one-shot, so this wires one saga subnet to the queue for one order. Many orders need one saga subnet each.

idioms.rationale: Release the worker when the saga commits.
idioms.caveat: Fires only on commit. If the saga rolls back, no port fires, the worker stays in in_use and the pool leaks a unit. Releasing on both outcomes is not expressible with the declared ports.

cites.note: CQ13: which port pairs in different patterns can a link join

cq13.expectation: Expect event candidates and no token candidates: the three patterns' place ports carry different schemas.

baez-master.title: Open Petri Nets
baez-master.use: Open Petri nets as cospans; composition is a pushout along boundary places.

bruni-et-al.authors: R. Bruni, H. Melgratti, U. Montanari, P. Sobociński
bruni-et-al.title: Connector algebras for C/E and P/T nets' interactions
bruni-et-al.use: Nets with boundaries: composition synchronises transitions on a shared boundary. The semantics of event links.

coecke-duncan.title: Interacting Quantum Observables: Categorical Algebra and Diagrammatics
coecke-duncan.use: ZX-calculus spiders and the spider-fusion rule. Only the fusion shape is borrowed here.

spivak-wd.title: The operad of wiring diagrams: formalizing a graphical language for databases, recursion, and plug-and-play circuits
spivak-wd.use: Boxes with typed ports nested in an outer box; filling a hole is operadic composition.

fong-spivak.title: Seven Sketches in Compositionality: An Invitation to Applied Category Theory
fong-spivak.use: Wiring diagrams and operads, introductory treatment.

selinger.title: A survey of graphical languages for monoidal categories
selinger.use: String diagrams: boxes are morphisms, wires are objects, side by side is the tensor, stacking is composition.

baez-gms.authors: J. C. Baez, F. Genovese, J. Master, M. Shulman
baez-gms.title: Categories of Nets
baez-gms.use: Petri nets generate monoidal categories; a run of a net is a morphism (a process).

ghani-hedges.authors: Neil Ghani, Jules Hedges, Viktor Winschel, Philipp Zahn
ghani-hedges.title: Compositional Game Theory
ghani-hedges.use: Open games as lenses: play flows forward, utility flows back. Here only the shape is borrowed (an analogy).

cybercat.title: CyberCat Institute
cybercat.use: Categorical cybernetics. Linked for context; no claim on this page is attributed to it.

mei-douglas.title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
mei-douglas.use: As cited by the ontology ROADMAP Phase 4 (faithfulness checks). Title, authors and year checked against arXiv; its content is not summarised or relied on here.

psv-normal-forms.authors: E. Patterson, D. I. Spivak, D. Vagner
psv-normal-forms.title: Wiring diagrams as normal forms for computing in symmetric monoidal categories
psv-normal-forms.use: Directed acyclic wiring diagrams as an unbiased representation of morphisms in a symmetric monoidal category: the interchange law holds identically, so two drawings of one composite compare without rewriting. Grounds reading the wiring and string views as one morphism.

catlab.authors: M. Halter, E. Patterson, A. Baas, J. Fairbanks
catlab.title: Compositional Scientific Computing with Catlab and SemanticModels
catlab.use: Prior art: Catlab.jl, software that composes models of interconnected systems as cospan algebras. Related work only; nothing on this page uses Catlab.

meseguer-montanari.title: Petri nets are monoids
meseguer-montanari.use: Markings as elements of the free commutative monoid on places, and a net's computations as a monoidal category. Background for the firing rule and for reading a marking as a multiset.

sobocinski-2010.title: Representations of Petri Net Interactions
sobocinski-2010.use: Petri nets with boundaries, composed by synchronising transitions across a shared boundary: the earlier presentation of the composition that bruni-et-al develops.

joyal-street.title: The geometry of tensor calculus, I
joyal-street.use: Soundness of string diagrams for monoidal categories: deforming a diagram does not change the morphism it denotes, which is why a view may re-lay-out a composite without changing its meaning.

chyp.title: Chyp: an interactive theorem prover for string diagrams
chyp.use: String-diagram rewriting over cospans of hypergraphs (per its README). Used as the checker for the composition-law theory exported under chyp/; what it checked is recorded there, not here. No paper describing Chyp itself was found on arXiv, so only the repository is cited.

coecke-kissinger.title: Picturing Quantum Processes: A First Course in Quantum Theory and Diagrammatic Reasoning
coecke-kissinger.use: Textbook treatment of spiders and spider fusion; an alternative reference to coecke-duncan for the fusion shape borrowed for sync.
